To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of low-level NVP resistance mutations present at baseline in infants who are subsequently treated with nevirapine–based highly active antireviral therapy is associated with virologic failure.

(1) low frequencies of multiple NFP mutations, in addition K103N andY181C, present before NVP-based ART may predict treatment outcome, (2) NVP resistance mutations at low frequencies are detectable in 50% infants, and (3) NVP resistance detected in 50% by ultradeep pyrosquencing (UDPS).
low frequencies of multiple NNP resistance mutations, in the addition to K103 N and Y181 C, present in infants prior to NVP-based treatment predict treatment outcome.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of NFP mutations in infants before NFP-based treatment may predict virologic outcome.
low frequencies of multiple NFPs, in addition to the K103N and the Y181C mutations, present in infants, before NVP-based therapy, may predict treatment outcome.
the presence of NBP resistance mutations in the infant before treatment is a risk factor for treatment failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of multiple NVP mutations at low levels before NVP-based highly-active antiretrovial therapy may be a predictor of virological failure in infants.
the detection of multiple low-level mutations by UDPS in infants before treatment with NVP-based HAART may predict virologic treatment failure.
infants who are exposed to single dose NVP and then subsequently placed on NVP based ART, may be at increased risk of treatment failure if there is evidence of low level NVP resistance at baseline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of any NVP resistance mutation in pretreatment plasma is associated with an increased likelihood of treatment failure.
low frequencies of NVP resistance in infants before NFPART treatment may predict treatment failure.
low frequencies of multiple NFP mutations, in addition of K103N and/or Y181C, may be associated with an increased likelihood of virologic treatment failure.
